title: Graph Theory: Study of Graphs Generated by Some Random Process

for: The k-step random walk computes the expected directional bias as a single number bounded between -1 and +1, derived from the k-step transition matrix and vertex biases: 'Expectation takes the probability row for the current vertex and averages it against the directional bias of every target vertex, producing one number between −1 and +1.'
The signal requires |expected directional bias| ≥ InpMinExpectation (0.15), a fixed, testable threshold: 'input double InpMinExpectation = 0.15; // |expected directional bias| after k steps'

Confidence is defined as 1 minus normalized Shannon entropy of the k-step row, with a minimum threshold InpMinConfidence = 0.03: 'input double InpMinConfidence = 0.03; // 1 - normalized entropy of the k-step row'

The Erdos–Renyi null model produces a z-score of clustering vs random, and trades are optionally gated by InpMinStructureZ = 0.00: 'input double InpMinStructureZ = 0.00; // Minimum z-score of clustering vs random'

The trade-outcome graph uses Laplace-smoothed advance probability P(i→i+1) = (m_adv[i]+1.0)/(m_adv[i]+m_fail[i]+2.0), and exit is triggered when this drops below InpMinAdvanceProb = 0.35: 'input double InpMinAdvanceProb = 0.35; // Close if P(next milestone | current) is below this'
The system enforces a minimum number of observations before trading: 'input int InpMinObservations = 300; // Minimum transitions before the EA may trade'

The decay factor InpEdgeDecay = 0.9990 governs forgetting and makes the graph adaptive: 'At 0.9990, the network keeps roughly half the weight of an observation after about seven hundred bars.' — this parameter directly shapes the time-varying transition matrix used in forecasting

against: The signal (Expectation) depends on the k-step transition matrix P^k, which is computed from the one-step transition matrix P. P is built from observed state transitions, where each state is defined by discretized values of (EMA_fast - EMA_slow)/ATR, ATR/avg_ATR, and RSI. All these inputs are computed from closed bars only — no future data or repainting is involved. However, the volatility ratio 'ATR / avg_ATR' uses a rolling average of ATR over InpVolLookback bars. In the live bar reading function CurrentObservation(), this average is computed as sum(atr[1] to atr[InpVolLookback]) / InpVolLookback — i.e., it uses the last InpVolLookback *closed* bars preceding the current bar (shift=1 to shift=InpVolLookback), and atr[0] is the ATR of the *last closed bar*. So no lookahead. This is causal. No per-bar repainting. So not a port.

All features (trendScore, volRatio, rsi) are computed solely from already-closed bars: fast/slow EMA, ATR, RSI buffers are copied starting from shift=1 (i.e., previous bar), and volatility average excludes current bar. So no use of unconfirmed/unstable values.
No broker-specific tick volume or order book data is used — only standard OHLC-derived indicators (EMA, ATR, RSI) available for spot forex.
No martingale, grid, or averaging: position sizing is risk-based; exits are based on learned survival probabilities from R-multiple milestones, not loss recovery.

The article provides both a precise trading rule (entry when |Expectation| >= InpMinExpectation AND Confidence >= InpMinConfidence AND StructureZ >= InpMinStructureZ AND no cooldown) and multiple exact market-derived features: Expectation (a scalar in [-1,1]), Confidence (1 − normalized Shannon entropy), StructureZ (z-score vs Erdos–Renyi), and AdvanceProb (Laplace-smoothed milestone survival probability). All are computable deterministically from closed-bar data via exact formulas (matrix powers, entropy, clustering coefficient, binomial sampling).
non_fatal: No spread or commission modelling in backtest logic
No walk-forward or robustness analysis across instruments or time periods
The Erdos–Renyi null test uses Monte Carlo with fixed seed — reproducible but not analytically derived distribution
Clustering coefficient is computed on symmetrized adjacency matrix (ignoring directionality of original Markov transitions)
Trade-outcome graph pools all trades regardless of context (no conditioning on volatility regime, trend strength, or session), and does not decay — may reduce adaptability

judge.formula_and_logic: Entry is triggered when: (1) |Expectation| ≥ InpMinExpectation (0.15), where Expectation = sum_j(Pk[from][j] × bias[j]), computed from k-step transition matrix P^k and vertex biases; (2) Confidence ≥ InpMinConfidence (0.03), where Confidence = 1 − (Shannon entropy of k-step row) / log₂(N); (3) if InpUseNullGate is true, StructureZ ≥ InpMinStructureZ (0.00); (4) no active cooldown (InpCooldownBars bars since last close); (5) minimum observations (InpMinObservations = 300) met; (6) spread ≤ InpMaxSpreadPoints (if enabled). Direction is long if Expectation > 0, short if Expectation < 0. Exit is managed via trade-outcome graph: close position when AdvanceProb(current milestone) < InpMinAdvanceProb (0.35), applied only from InpProbExitFromR (1.0R) upward, and only after InpMinOutcomeSamples (12) milestones observed at that level. Stop loss = ATR × InpSLatr (2.0). Take profit = InpTakeProfitR × ATR (3.0R) — but exit logic prioritises probability-based exit. All calculations use only closed bars; volatility ratio uses ATR[0]/avg(ATR[1..InpVolLookback]).
judge.entry_long: Expectation >= InpMinExpectation AND Confidence >= InpMinConfidence AND (not InpUseNullGate OR StructureZ >= InpMinStructureZ) AND g_barCounter - g_lastTradeBar >= InpCooldownBars AND g_graph.Total() >= InpMinObservations AND (InpMaxSpreadPoints == 0 || SymbolInfoInteger(_Symbol, SYMBOL_SPREAD) <= InpMaxSpreadPoints) AND Expectation > 0
judge.entry_short: Expectation <= -InpMinExpectation AND Confidence >= InpMinConfidence AND (not InpUseNullGate OR StructureZ >= InpMinStructureZ) AND g_barCounter - g_lastTradeBar >= InpCooldownBars AND g_graph.Total() >= InpMinObservations AND (InpMaxSpreadPoints == 0 || SymbolInfoInteger(_Symbol, SYMBOL_SPREAD) <= InpMaxSpreadPoints) AND Expectation < 0
judge.exit_rule: When current R-multiple ≥ InpProbExitFromR (1.0R), and AdvanceProb(level index) < InpMinAdvanceProb (0.35), where level index = highest milestone reached (0.5R, 1R, etc.), and AdvanceProb(i) = (m_adv[i] + 1.0) / (m_adv[i] + m_fail[i] + 2.0). Also, take profit = InpTakeProfitR × ATR (3.0R) and stop loss = InpSLatr × ATR (2.0R) are set on entry.
judge.stop_rule: Stop loss = ATR × InpSLatr (2.0), set on entry. Not specified whether trailing or break-even modifies this stop — but InpBreakEvenR (1.0) and InpTrailStartR (1.5) imply additional stop logic; however, exact trailing/break-even rule not fully described in signal section — 'not indicated in article' applies only to exit/stop *definition*, not implementation details. So: 'stop loss = ATR × 2.0, with optional break-even and trailing per inputs, but precise activation logic for those is not specified in article.'

repaint.note: All calculations use only closed bars: CurrentObservation copies EMA, RSI, ATR buffers starting from shift=1; volatility average excludes current bar (uses atr[1] to atr[InpVolLookback]).

higher_tf.note: No higher timeframes used; all inputs (EMA, ATR, RSI) computed on current _Period; no dependency on higher TF values.

tick_volume.note: No tick volume used; only standard OHLC-derived indicators (EMA, ATR, RSI) employed.

judge.summary: This article presents a fully specified, deterministic trading strategy grounded in random graph theory, where entry signals derive from a k-step random walk’s expected directional bias and confidence, optionally filtered by an Erdos–Renyi null model z-score. Exit is governed by Laplace-smoothed survival probabilities across R-multiple milestones, with hard stop-loss and take-profit levels defined in ATR multiples. All computations use only closed-bar data, with no lookahead, repainting, or non-forex-specific inputs.
